output.brief:
The price rise is not what's driving the extra cancellations. The cause is the Quillbook connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then our fallback route has sometimes reported success without writing the invoice, and retries sometimes post it twice. Our monitoring only counts errors, so it shows green. About 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts have had missing or duplicate invoices, and 34% of them cancelled, against 8% of those with no failures. Churn at Quillbook accounts with the price lock, who saw no price rise, jumped just as much (1.9% to 5.9%). Accounts with no connector are flat at about 1.9%, whatever their price or size. The "bigger increase, more churn" pattern arises because Quillbook accounts have more seats. Seasonality and the mobile release don't fit the data. Tallymarsh looks small and within normal variation, but its log hasn't been reviewed.

Recommendations:
- Make the Quillbook fix to the new interface (3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority, and contact every affected account, including those who cancelled, to correct their invoices.
- Keep the duplicate-invoice hold. It has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books.
- Don't roll back the price, which would cost about $220k a month.
- Have someone review the Tallymarsh log before committing a rebuild team.

I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
